questions.q: A five-task run fails at task 3. What does Repair run re-run?

options.t: All five tasks, from the beginning
options.why: Repair re-runs only the unsuccessful tasks and their dependents.

options.t: Only task 3, never its dependents
options.why: Dependents of the failed task are re-run too.

options.t: Task 3 and the tasks that depend on it
Only tasks that succeeded, to confirm their results
options.why: Successful tasks aren't re-run.

questions.explain: Repair re-runs only the unsuccessful tasks and their dependents; successful tasks and those depending only on them aren't re-run.

questions.q: A task failed because of a bug. You fix the notebook, then repair the run. Which version runs?

options.t: The fixed notebook: repairs use the current job and task settings
The original notebook, frozen at the time of the failed run
options.why: Unsuccessful tasks re-run with the current settings.

options.t: Neither: a repair only re-checks the task's output
options.why: A repair re-runs the task.

options.t: The fixed notebook, but only if the job is recreated first
options.why: No recreation is needed; repair uses current settings.

questions.explain: Unsuccessful tasks are re-run with the current job and task settings, so fix first, then repair.

questions.q: A task appended half its rows to a table, then failed. The run is repaired. What is the risk?

options.t: None: repair resumes the task from the row where it stopped
options.why: A repaired task restarts from the beginning.

options.t: None: Lakeflow Jobs makes every task idempotent
options.why: Lakeflow Jobs doesn't make tasks idempotent.

options.t: The repaired task appends all its rows again, duplicating the first half
The table is rolled back automatically before the repair
options.why: Nothing is rolled back automatically.

questions.explain: A repair re-runs each unsuccessful task from the beginning, and Lakeflow Jobs doesn't make tasks idempotent; a task that wrote part of its output can duplicate it. Use overwrite or merge rather than append.

questions.q: A single-task job failed. How is it run again?

options.t: With Repair run, like any other job
options.why: Repair needs two or more tasks.

options.t: With Run now
By deleting and recreating the job
options.why: Run now re-runs it.

options.t: By restoring the job's last successful version
options.why: Run now re-runs it.

questions.explain: Repair is supported only for jobs with two or more tasks; a single-task job is re-run with Run now.

questions.q: Several tasks share a job cluster. The run fails and is repaired. Which cluster does the repair use?

options.t: The same job cluster, kept running for the repair
options.why: A repair run creates a new job cluster.

options.t: Any all-purpose cluster the user is attached to
options.why: A repair creates a new job cluster.

options.t: A serverless cluster, regardless of the job's settings
options.why: A repair creates a new job cluster.

options.t: A new job cluster

questions.q: In a job's matrix view, what does a pink task bar mean?

options.why: Green is success.

options.t: The task failed
options.why: Red is failure.

options.t: The task was skipped

questions.q: A task in last night's run failed. Where do you find its error message?

options.t: In the pipeline event log of the workspace

options.t: In the task run details, opened from the run's matrix view

options.t: In system.billing.usage for that run

questions.explain: Open the job's Runs tab and matrix view, then click the failed task: its task run details show the output, error message and metadata.

questions.q: A job-level failure notification is set, and a task fails then succeeds on retry. Is a failure notification sent?

options.t: Yes, for every failed attempt
options.why: Job-level notifications aren't sent when failed tasks are retried.

options.t: Only if the retry also fails
options.why: To hear about every failed attempt, use task notifications.

options.t: No: job-level notifications aren't sent for retried tasks
Yes, but only by email
options.why: Retried task failures don't send job-level notifications by any channel.

questions.explain: Job-level notifications aren't sent when failed tasks are retried; for a notification after every failed task, use task notifications.

questions.q: Which events can a job notification be set for?

options.t: Duration exceeding a threshold
Streaming backlog exceeding a threshold
A grant changed on a table the job reads
options.why: That isn't a job notification event.

options.t: The workspace's DBU budget being reached
options.why: That isn't a job notification event.

options.t: A schema change on a source table
options.why: That isn't a job notification event.

questions.explain: Notifications can be set for start, success, failure, duration over a threshold, streaming backlog over a threshold, and maintenance start and end for continuous jobs.

questions.q: Which destinations can job notifications go to?

options.t: Email only
options.why: Admin-configured destinations such as Slack, Teams, PagerDuty and webhooks are also supported.

options.why: Notifications go to email or system destinations.

questions.q: A run ends in the state 'Succeeded with failures'. Which notification does it trigger?

options.t: Failure
options.why: It counts as a successful state.

options.t: Success
None
options.why: It counts as success, so success notifications fire.

options.t: Duration warning

questions.q: A job should continue to the publish step only if a data quality query finds no bad rows. Which task can evaluate that?

A dashboard task, which refreshes the quality dashboard first

options.why: An alert task evaluates the condition.

options.t: A pipeline task with no expectations

questions.explain: A Databricks SQL alert can run as a job task so condition checks run in the pipeline and downstream tasks can branch on the result.

questions.q: What states can a Databricks SQL alert evaluation resolve to?

OK, UNKNOWN or FAILED

options.t: PASSED or FAILED only

options.t: GREEN, AMBER or RED
options.why: The states are OK, TRIGGERED and ERROR.

questions.q: Which practice makes a job task safe to retry or repair?

options.t: Appending its results to the target table every time it runs
options.why: A rerun would append again and duplicate rows.

options.t: Writing results only after a long sleep, so earlier attempts finish
options.why: Timing doesn't make a task idempotent.

options.t: Overwriting the range it owns or merging on a key
Running it on all-purpose compute so state is kept between attempts
options.why: Compute type doesn't make a write idempotent.

questions.explain: Because repairs re-run tasks from the start and retries rerun them, tasks should overwrite what they own or merge on keys, not blindly append.

questions.q: Which compute should a scheduled production job run on?

options.why: Databricks doesn't recommend all-purpose compute for production jobs.

options.t: Job compute or serverless jobs compute
A SQL warehouse for every task type, including Python
options.why: SQL warehouses run SQL tasks; jobs use job or serverless compute.

options.t: Whatever cluster the job's creator last used interactively

questions.explain: Databricks recommends job compute (or serverless jobs compute) for scheduled work; on job failure and retry, new compute resources deploy.

questions.q: Several streaming tasks run in one continuous job. One fails while the others keep running. What can happen if task retry mode isn't 'On failure'?

options.t: The job restarts immediately and all streams resume
options.why: Without On failure, the job waits until all tasks have failed.

options.t: The failed stream retries on its own every minute
options.why: It retries on its own only with Task retry mode On failure.

options.t: The other streams are stopped so the job can restart cleanly
options.why: They keep running; the job doesn't restart until all fail.

options.t: The failed stream stays down while the job looks healthy

questions.explain: In a multi-task continuous job, a failed task retries on its own only if Task retry mode is On failure; otherwise the job doesn't start a new run until all other tasks also fail.

options.why: Databricks recommends the Continuous job trigger for streaming workloads.

options.t: As a manual run that someone restarts after failures

On an all-purpose cluster with autoscaling enabled

questions.explain: Schedule streams as Lakeflow Jobs on jobs compute using Continuous mode, which prevents concurrent runs, starts a new run after failure and uses exponential backoff.

questions.q: Why shouldn't a streaming notebook run as a Lakeflow job call awaitTermination()?

options.t: The Jobs service already keeps the run alive, and the call blocks it from tracking the query
It makes the stream run in batch mode instead of streaming
options.why: It blocks the notebook; it doesn't change the mode.

options.t: It deletes the checkpoint when the query ends
options.why: It doesn't touch the checkpoint.

options.t: It isn't available on Databricks at all
options.why: It exists; it just shouldn't be used in jobs.

questions.explain: In Lakeflow Jobs, don't use awaitTermination(): the Jobs service prevents a run completing while a query is active, and the call blocks the service from tracking the query (streaming backlog notifications need that).

questions.q: A continuous job keeps failing. What does Lakeflow Jobs do?

options.t: Stops the job permanently after the third failure
options.why: It retries with exponential backoff.

options.t: Retries with exponential backoff; Restart run resets it

options.t: Deletes the job's checkpoints and starts fresh

questions.explain: When consecutive failures of a continuous job exceed a threshold, Lakeflow Jobs uses exponential backoff; the job page shows consecutive failures and the next retry, and Restart run resets it.
